main_text.p: Medicinam facilitantes hac pestilentia seminaria confundere, parum referre existimantes, num pestis sit hominis, aerus, aqua vel terra.Censura
Quidam falsò opinantur pestis contagium ex aere e semper primario effundi. Verum de his & similibus Pseudodoxis in tractatu meo de peste prolixè disserui.
Unum hic meminisse oportet, pestis vocabulum equinocum[?] esse, aerium enim venenum, morbum ab eo illatum, nec non bubonem morbi comites, (a quibus rursus diuersa est febris pestilens) denotat.

page.notes: The right-margin notes "Pestis propriè quid?", "Febris pestilens quid? eiusque essentia? &qua ratione febris pestilens à peste cōcitetur?" are split across lines by the narrow column; I reassembled them in order. Doubtful readings: "aerus" (line 1, possibly a printing error for aëris), "equinocum" (possibly equinoctium), "nonnũquã le" (line-end abbreviation hard to read; may be nonnunquam ... ), and the page number "31" (the 1 is faint). The right-margin notes are shown inline where they stand, not as separate paragraphs. The top-right "Censura" is a side note on the first line.
